title: Viral Nanoparticles for In vivo Tumor Imaging
protocol: Set the indoor plant chamber controls to 15 hours of day with 100% light, 25 °C, and 65% humidity.
Set the indoor plant chamber controls to 9 hours of night with 0% light, 22 °C, and 60% humidity.
Plant 3 cowpea seeds per pot on Day 0.
Plant approximately 30 N. benthamiana seeds per pot on Day 0.
Fertilize plants once a week with 1 tablespoon fertilizer diluted in 5 liters of water.
Re-pot N. benthamiana to 1 plant per pot on Day 14.
Infect the primary leaves with CPMV using 5 μg/50 μl per leaf by mechanical inoculation and a light dusting of carborundum on Day 10.
Infect three to five leaves with PVX, TMV, or BMV using 5 μg/50 μl per leaf by mechanical inoculation and a light dusting of carborundum on Day 28.
Harvest cowpea leaves and store them at -80 °C on Day 20.
Harvest N. benthamiana leaves and store them at -80 °C on Day 42.
Homogenize 100 g of frozen leaves using a standard blender with 2 volumes of cold buffer.
Filter the homogenized leaf mixture through 2-3 layers of cheesecloth.
Adjust pH to 6.5 for PVX purification using 1 M HCl.
Add 0.2% (w/v) ascorbic acid and 0.2% (w/v) sodium sulfite for PVX.
Centrifuge the crude plant homogenate at 5,500 x g for 20 minutes.
Collect the supernatant after centrifugation.
Layer 25 ml of supernatant over 5 ml of 10% (w/v) sucrose solution for BMV.
Centrifuge the mixture at 9,000 x g for 3 hr and resuspend pellets in 38.5% CsCl solution (w/v).
Mix by shaking for 5 hr.
Extract plant material by adding 0.7 volumes of 1:1 (v/v) chloroform:1-butanol.
Stir the mixture for 30-60 min.
Centrifuge the solution at 5,500 x g for 20 min and collect the upper aqueous phase.
Add NaCl to 0.2 M and 8% (w/v) PEG (MW 8,000).
For TMV, also add 1% (v/v) Triton X-100.
Stir the mixture for at least 1 hr, then let sit for at least 1 hr.
Centrifuge the solution at 15,000 x g for 15 min and resuspend pellet in 10 ml of buffer.
For PVX, add 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol and urea to 0.5 M.
Centrifuge the mixture at 8,000 x g for 30 min and collect supernatant.
Ultracentrifuge the supernatant at 160,000 x g for 3 hr.
Resuspend pellet in 5 ml buffer overnight.
Prepare a 10-40% sucrose gradient using equal volumes of 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40% sucrose in buffer (heaviest first).
Allow the gradient to equilibrate overnight at room temperature.
Ultracentrifuge resuspended pellet over sucrose gradient at 100,000 x g for 2 hr (24 hr for BMV).
Collect light scattering band and dialyze against buffer.
Characterize VNPs and store at 4 °C.
For long-term storage, store at -80 °C.
Perform UV/visible spectroscopy to determine the concentration of VNPs.
Measure the absorbance of 2 μl of sample using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Determine the concentration of particles and dyes using the Beer-Lambert law.
Analyze particles by size-exclusion fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC).
Load 50-100 μg of VNPs in 200 μl of 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer onto a Superose 6 size-exclusion column.
Set detectors to 260 nm, 280 nm, and the excitation wavelength of any dyes attached.
Run the chromatography at a flow rate of 0.5 ml/min for 72 min.
Evaluate the elution profile and A260:A280 nm ratio to assess purity and integrity of VNP preparation.
Perform denaturing Bis-Tris polyacrylamide 4-12% gradient gel electrophoresis.
Add 3 ml of 4x LDS sample buffer to 10 μg of the particles in 9 μl of potassium phosphate buffer.
Add 1 μl of 4x LDS sample buffer and 3 μl of β-mercaptoethanol to BMV.
Incubate in heat block for 5 min at 100 °C.
Load samples onto an SDS gel.
Run samples at 200 V for 1 hr in 1x MOPS running buffer.
Document the gel under UV light to visualize fluorescent coat proteins.
Stain non-fluorescent protein with Coomassie blue (0.25% (w/v) Coomassie Brilliant Blue R-250, 30% (v/v) methanol, 10% (v/v) acetic acid) for 1 hr.
Destain with 30% methanol, 10% acetic acid overnight. Change the solution if required.
Document the gel under white light.
Dilute samples to 0.1-1 mg/ml in 20 μl of DI water.
Place 20 μl drops of the samples on Parafilm.
Cover drops with a TEM grid and let sit for 2 min.
Wick off the excess solution on the grid with filter paper.
Wash grid by placing on a drop of DI water then wicking dry.
Stain grid by placing on a 20 μl drop of 2% (w/v) uranyl acetate for 2 min.
Wick off the excess stain with filter paper.
Wash grid once more in water.
Observe grid under a transmission electron microscope.
Add 2,500 molar equivalents of Alexa Fluor 647 succinimidyl ester and 4,500 equivalents of NHS-PEG (M.W. 5,000) dissolved in DMSO to CPMV in 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer.
Adjust the buffer and DMSO volumes such that the final concentration of CPMV is 2 mg/ml and DMSO content is 10% of the total reaction volume.
Incubate the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature protected from light.
Add a 10,000 molar excess of NHS-dye and NHS-PEG to PVX in 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer.
Adjust the buffer and DMSO volumes such that the final concentration of PVX is 2 mg/ml and DMSO content is 10% of the total reaction volume.
Incubate the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature protected from light.
Mix 400 μl of 0.3 M p-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate, 25 μl of 3.0 M sodium nitrite, and 75 μl of 0.68 M distilled 3-ethynylaniline dissolved in acetonitrile at 4 °C for 1 hr.
Add 3.3 ml of borate buffer, pH 8.8, containing 100 mM NaCl to 1.25 ml of TMV (20 mg/ml stock solution).
React the TMV with 450 μl of diazonium salt (alkyne) solution in an ice bath for 3 hr.
Purify the final product using a sucrose cushion.
Attach azide-functional Alexa Fluor 647 and PEG-azide (M.W. 5,000) to TMV using copper(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC).
Add 2 equivalents of dye- and PEG-azide per coat protein.
Incubate the reaction mixture with 1 mM CuSO4, 2 mM AMG, and 2 mM sodium ascorbate at room temperature for 15 min.
Adjust the buffer volume to achieve a final reaction concentration of TMV at 2 mg/ml.
Add 2,000 molar equivalents of Oregon Green 488 succinimidyl ester dissolved in DMSO to cBMV in TNKM buffer.
Incubate the reaction mixture overnight at 4 °C protected from light.
Purify particles using centrifugal filters.
Add 2,000 molar excess of PEG-maleimide.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 2 hr at 4 °C.
Pass the solution through a 40% (w/v) sucrose cushion at 160,000 x g for 2.5 hr.
Re-dissolve the pellet in buffer.
Alternatively, dialyze against appropriate buffer using 10 kDa cut-off spin filters.
Culture HT-29 human colon cancer cells in RPMI medium supplemented with 5% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 1% L-glutamine at 37 °C in 5% CO2.
Wash cells twice with sterile PBS.
Incubate the cells with 5 ml of trypsin-EDTA at 37 °C for 5 min to harvest them.
Inactivate the trypsin with 5 ml of RPMI medium.
Collect cells by centrifuging at 500 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the cells in fresh RPMI at 5x10^6 cells/50 μl medium.
Mix the resuspended cells with an equal volume of matrigel prior to injection.
Procure six-week old NCR nu/nu mice.
Maintain the mice on an alfalfa-free diet for 2 weeks.
Induce tumor xenografts by subcutaneously injecting 5x106 cells/100 μl/tumor in the flanks using a 18 1/2 gauge sterile needle.
Monitor the animals regularly.
Measure the tumor size using calipers.
Allow the tumors to grow to an average volume of 20 mm3 within the next 12 days.
Assign mice to two different groups randomly: PBS and VNP (n = 3 animals/group/time point).
Administer by intravenous tail vein injection 100 μl of sterile PBS or 10 mg/kg VNP formulation using a 1 ml 28 gauge insulin syringe.
Sacrifice mice at different time points (2, 24, and 72 hours) using CO2 gas.
Dissect the animals and excise all major organs including brain, heart, lungs, spleen, kidneys, liver, and tumors on the flanks.
Place the tissues on parafilm and analyze with fluorescence imaging instrument using yellow excitation and emission filters (800 ms exposure).
Save the images and analyze fluorescent intensities using ImageJ 1.44o software.
Cut each tissue in half and embed one half in OCT compound for cryo-sectioning and confocal analysis.
Collect the other half in pre-weighed cryo-vials and immediately freeze them using liquid N2.
Store frozen tissues at -80°C until ready for further processing.
Thaw frozen tissues at room temperature and place them in separate 50 ml Falcon tubes containing 1 ml of PBS.
Using a handheld tissue homogenizer, homogenize the tissues for 2-3 minutes in PBS.
Transfer the homogenate to microfuge tubes.
Centrifuge the homogenates for 10 minutes at 13,000 x g to remove non-homogenized tissue.
Pipette 100 μl of the supernatant from the tissues into a 384 well black UV plate.
Evaluate fluorescence intensity using a plate reader at Ex/Em wavelengths 600/665.
Normalize the obtained fluorescent values by the tissue weights.
Prepare cryo-microtome sections (10 μm) and store them at -20 °C.
Stain tissue sections for cell nuclei with DAPI.
Stain tissue sections for endothelial cells using FITC-labeled anti-mouse CD31 antibody.
Carry out confocal microscopy analysis to map the vascular and intra-tumoral localization of fluorescently-labeled VNPs.
